executiveSummary: The period is dominated by catastrophic flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border, concurrent large wildfires in the western United States, and typhoon-driven flooding in southern China. Secondary hazards and access constraints continue to elevate operational risk. Himalayan flood catastrophe: Reporting varies but indicates at least 390-633+ fatalities and 1,400-3,000 missing across Nepal and Tibet after a glacier-collapse flood swept through mountain corridors. View Article Supporting Report Upstream barrier lake instability is disrupting rescues and could trigger further flooding; authorities briefly halted operations amid renewed overflow risk. View Article Children and vulnerable groups: UNICEF/aid agencies warn at least 17,000 children urgently need assistance as communities remain cut off. View Article Access/infrastructure: Roads, bridges, and buildings were washed out or buried; more than 100 people were trapped at a hydropower tunnel during response. View Article Humanitarian financing: IFRC released emergency funds and launched an appeal to support lifesaving assistance in northern Nepal. Supporting Report United States - Reno, Nevada: A fast-moving wildfire destroyed 30+ homes; 42,000 were under evacuation orders (about 90,000 urged), with at least six injuries and large-scale sheltering. View Article United States - North Central Texas: A rapidly expanding wildfire (78+ square miles in View Article China - Guangxi and south: Typhoon Narra caused widespread flooding and mass evacuations, with heavier rain expected to worsen conditions. View Article Hawaii: Post-hurricane heavy rain risk persisted with two storm-related deaths and concerns for repeat flooding in vulnerable areas. View Article

outlook72h: Himalayan Flood Zone (Nepal-Tibet) Expect fluctuating access windows due to barrier lake overflow potential; maintain no-regrets posture on evacuation triggers near unstable slopes and river corridors. Security Advisory Prioritize air bridges where feasible; pre-stage high-clearance assets for debris-blocked routes. View Article Other Priority Areas Reno, Nevada: Continued fire behavior possible; maintain shelter capacity and redundancy for power interruptions. View Article Southern China: Additional heavy rain forecast-anticipate extended evacuations and WASH needs in submerged communities. View Article Hawaii: Maintain flash flood/mudslide readiness in steep terrain and burn scars; monitor renewed rain bands. View Article Japan (Okinawa/Amami/Kagoshima): Residual outage and landslide risks amid storm passage; monitor for cascading transport impacts. View Article
